blocks.text: A 2020 census tract in north-central Allen County: 28.896 square miles of land, internal point 40.8240378, -84.1599836. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), national tract file. Allen County holds 35 tracts in the 2020 geography. [verified] — same source.

**It is 98.5% of Sugar Creek Township plus a fifth of American Township.** Of its 107 blocks, 90 fall in [Sugar Creek](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml) — 82.1% of the tract's land, 1,192 people — and 17 in [American](../place/american-township.yml) — 17.9%, 408 people. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), block composition; the block areas sum to the tract's own `AREALAND` exactly, which is the check that they are all of it.

It holds all but 0.372 square miles of Sugar Creek and adds 5.175 of American, so a figure published for this tract and read as Sugar Creek Township's **overstates it by about a quarter** — 408 of 1,600 residents live in the other township. [inference]

nodes.label: Ohio's 4th congressional district (2020 geography)

blocks.text: The United States congressional district covering Allen County at the 2020 census. All 3,552 of the county's census blocks fall in it. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md). It runs to 4,665.374 square miles of land with an internal point at 40.387175, -83.935703. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md).

refusals: `effective_to` is absent because the corpus does not know the date the map was superseded, not because the district still stands as drawn.

blocks.text: The Ohio House of Representatives district covering Allen County under the map in force at the 2020 census. All 3,552 of the county's census blocks fall in it. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md).

**It is coterminous with the county.** Its gazetteer record reads `ALAND 1042587389`, `AWATER 11152061`, `ALAND_SQMI 402.545`, `INTPTLAT 40.771627`, `INTPTLONG -84.106103` — every field byte-identical to [Allen County](../place/allen-county.yml)'s own record in the county file. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md). Not approximately the same ground: the same ground.

The Ohio Senate district covering Allen County under the map in force at the 2020 census. All 3,552 of the county's census blocks fall in it, so the county is not split. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md).

Unlike [House District 4](ohio-house-district-4-2020.yml), it is much larger than the county: 2,659.11 square miles of land against the county's 402.545, with an internal point at 40.416995, -84.191133 that lies well south of Allen County's. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md). Allen County is roughly a seventh of it by land area. [inference]

A precinct of 1.548 square miles in northern Lima holding 3,240 people and 756 housing units, internal point 40.778293, -84.105936. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), layer 58.

**It is where three sources disagree with each other in a way that means something.** Its 908 registered voters are 0.28 per resident, the lowest of the county's 88 precincts against a median of 0.68 and a next-lowest of 0.54. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md) against TIGERweb block population. One of its 43 blocks holds 1,360 people in **zero** housing units, and set those aside and the ratio is 0.48 — low, and inside the range the rest of the county occupies.
It voted 287 to 234 for Trump over Biden on a 58.4 per cent turnout — nearly the county's most balanced precinct in a county that went 69 to 29. [verified] — OpenElections.

The single precinct covering [Sugar Creek Township](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml), holding 1,231 people and 515 housing units over 24.094 square miles, internal point 40.824171, -84.173844. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), layer 58.

**It is coterminous with the township.** The township's own gazetteer record gives 24.094 square miles of land and an internal point of 40.824171, -84.173843 — the same figures, differing in the last decimal place of the longitude by about four inches. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md). It is the only one of the county's 88 precincts that is a whole civil subdivision; four others are whole villages, and the remaining 83 are pieces.
The act of the Ohio General Assembly laying out Allen County in 1820 from the lands ceded at [St. Marys](treaty-of-st-marys.yml). [inference]

Laying out a county and organizing its government were separate acts in Ohio practice, often years apart: a county could exist on paper, attached to a neighbouring county for judicial and administrative purposes, before it had its own courts and officers. Allen County is understood to have been organized about a decade after it was created. [inference] — see [when Allen County's government was organized](../question/when-allen-county-was-organized.yml).
The well at Lima that struck oil in 1885 and opened the Lima–Indiana field. [inference] The drilling was after natural gas, following the Findlay boom to the north; oil is what came up. [inference]

The Lima crude was sour — high in sulphur, and difficult to refine into a saleable illuminant by the methods of the day. That property is why the field's development depended on a desulphurization process and hence on the capital and patents of [Standard Oil](../organization/standard-oil.yml) rather than on local operators. [inference]

The strike `affected` the county and not only the city: the Lima–Indiana field extended well beyond the corporate boundary, and the county's economy was reoriented from agriculture to petroleum and the manufacturing that followed it. [inference] That is why this node carries an `affected` edge to the county alongside its `occurred-in` edge to Lima — the two say different things, and only the first is true of the ground outside the city.

nodes.label: Removal of the Ottawa from the Auglaize and Ottawa river reserves

blocks.text: The removal of the Ottawa from their reserved lands in and near this county to territory west of the Mississippi, following further cession in the early 1830s. [inference]

properties.location_description: St. Marys, in present-day Auglaize County, Ohio. [inference]

blocks.text: The 1818 treaty negotiations at St. Marys, Ohio, by which Native nations ceded the remaining lands in northwest Ohio — the cession that made the ground Allen County was later laid out on available for survey and sale. [inference]

The cession also established reservations, including Ottawa reserves on the Auglaize and Ottawa rivers, which were themselves ceded and their occupants removed within about fifteen years — see [the Ottawa removal](ottawa-removal.yml). [inference]

properties.authority_source: An act of the Ohio General Assembly laying out the county from lands ceded at the Treaty of St. Marys. [inference] — the act itself has not been retrieved.

blocks.text: The county government: the unit of general-purpose government whose territory is [Allen County](../place/allen-county.yml). Ohio counties are administrative subdivisions of the state rather than home-rule corporations, and are governed by a three-member board of county commissioners alongside separately elected auditor, treasurer, recorder, sheriff, prosecutor, clerk of courts, coroner and engineer. [inference]

A district of 5,908 people over 72.263 square miles in the east of the county, internal point 40.721894, -83.954012, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

**It is the only one of the twelve whose name is not on any map of the county.** The other eleven carry the name of a village, a city or a township; this one carries the county's name and a compass direction, which is what a district looks like when it is assembled out of ground rather than grown from a town. It spans [Jackson Township](../place/jackson-township.yml) entire (3,143), [Auglaize Township](../place/auglaize-township.yml) all but 17 people (2,740), and 25 people of [Perry Township](../place/perry-township.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.

It holds three settlements and no large one: [Harrod](../place/harrod.yml) 423, [Lafayette](../place/lafayette.yml) 406, and [Westminster](../place/westminster.yml) 406 — 1,235 people in named places out of 5,908. [verified] — same source.

The township government whose territory is [Amanda Township](../place/amanda-township.yml). Its township house is at 690 S. Conant Road, its telephone is 419.647.6259, and its trustees meet on the first and third Wednesday of the month at 8:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.729304, -84.280797, landmarked `AMANDA TOWNSHIP HOUSE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

Its house carries a **Spencerville** postal address, and Spencerville is a village in [Spencer Township](../place/spencer-township.yml), not in this one. The county's own address file gives the building a blank `MUNI` — its answer for *in no municipality* — and the coordinate falls inside Amanda Township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), point-in-polygon against the 2020 county-subdivision layer.

The township government whose territory is [American Township](../place/american-township.yml). Its township house is at 102 Pioneer Road, its telephone is 419.331.8651, and its trustees meet on the second and last Monday of the month at 7:30 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.782867, -84.189127, landmarked `AMERICAN TOWNSHIP ADMINISTRATION BUILDING`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

It governs the county's most populous township — 14,538 people, more than any civil subdivision but [Lima](../place/lima.yml) — and the building is landmarked as an *administration building* rather than a township house, which is what a township of that size looks like in a county file. It runs its own fire service from two further addresses on Elida Road and Edgewood Drive, and a third station inside [Elida](../place/elida.yml). [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

The township government whose territory is [Auglaize Township](../place/auglaize-township.yml). Its township house is at 7726 Bellefontaine Road, its telephone is 419.648.7144, and its trustees meet on the first and third Monday of the month at 7:30 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.676380, -83.959923, landmarked `AUGLAIZE TOWNSHIP HOUSE & GARAGE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

Its territory holds two settlements, [Harrod](../place/harrod.yml) and [Westminster](../place/westminster.yml), and it is one of only two civil subdivisions in the county that gained population between 2020 and 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md).

A district of 12,101 people over 44.495 square miles north-east of Lima, internal point 40.79708, -84.060212, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

It lies wholly inside Allen County and is **not** the same ground as the township it is named for. All 9,399 people of [Bath Township](../place/bath-township.yml) are in it — 255 of the township's 256 blocks, the exception an unpopulated one that belongs to the Lima City district — but so are 1,573 residents of [Lima](../place/lima.yml) and 1,129 of [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml). A fifth of the district lives outside its namesake. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.
It contains one incorporated place, [Cairo](../place/cairo.yml) and its 517 people. [verified] — same source.

**Most of its Lima share is one block with no housing in it.** 1,360 of those 1,573 city residents are in census block `390030112001004`, which holds zero housing units — a group quarters, not a neighbourhood. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block layer. So the number of Lima *households* in this district is nearer 213 than 1,573, and [what stands on that block](../question/who-lives-in-the-county-without-housing.yml) is an open question.

The township government whose territory is [Bath Township](../place/bath-township.yml). Its township house is at 2880 Ada Road, its telephone is 419.221.1797, and its trustees meet on the first and third Tuesday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.759189, -84.051832, landmarked `BATH TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

The county's address file landmarks the building as `BATH TOWNSHIP BOARD OF TRUSTEES` and a township garage at the same address. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). That landmark is the closest thing in any retrieved source to a statement that the board exists as a body with a place to sit.
Its postal address is Lima, and the coordinate is inside Bath Township. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

A district of 6,438 people over 52.909 square miles in the county's north, internal point 40.865493, -83.95681, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

6,281 of its people are in Allen County and 157 in Hancock — it reaches **out** across the county line, which the district-level tally this node was first written from could not see. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Its Allen County ground is 5,832 people of [Richland Township](../place/richland-township.yml) and 449 of [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml).

**It does not hold all of Bluffton.** 3,875 of the village's 3,967 people are in it and 92 are in the Cory-Rawson Local district, on the Hancock County side. [verified] — same source. It also holds [Beaverdam](../place/beaverdam.yml) and its 319 people, six miles south-west, which is the older fact this node was missing: the district is named for one village and serves two.

The municipal corporation governing [Delphos](../place/delphos.yml), the county's second city. **It is the only municipality here made by merger**: the county records that Delphos was originally four towns — Howard, Section Ten, West Bredeick and East Bredeick — which combined into one in 1851. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page.

Its territory crosses the Allen–Van Wert county line, and its 7,117 people divide 3,935 in Allen and 3,182 in Van Wert. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population and [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md). It is therefore the second corporation in this corpus, after [the Village of Bluffton](village-of-bluffton.yml), whose ground is not contained by one county — and unlike Bluffton, whose village is split between two school districts, this city's schools follow the corporation across the line entire.

The municipal corporation governing [Lima](../place/lima.yml). Under Ohio law a municipality becomes a city rather than a village when its population passes 5,000, and it may adopt a home-rule charter; Lima has long been past that threshold. [inference]

A Putnam County district that reaches into Allen — 5,120 people over 73.137 square miles, internal point 40.907866, -84.118198, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

4,631 of its people are in Putnam County and 489 in Allen — 9.6 per cent. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. The Allen County portion is 44 blocks in the north of [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml) and contains no incorporated place.

A district of 9,903 people over 53.041 square miles on the county's western edge, internal point 40.829646, -84.35015, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

**It is a Van Wert County district as much as an Allen County one.** 5,696 of its people are in Allen County and 4,207 in Van Wert — 57 per cent against 43. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Its Allen County ground is 5,547 people of [Marion Township](../place/marion-township.yml) and 149 of [Spencer Township](../place/spencer-township.yml).

It holds the whole of [Delphos](../place/delphos.yml) — all 7,117 people on both sides of the county line, in one district. [verified] — same source. That is the fact worth keeping: the city is split between two counties and its schools are not. Where a municipal boundary and a county boundary disagree, the school district followed the municipality.

The county's second most populous school district — 18,876 people over 67.454 square miles, internal point 40.804278, -84.199108, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

It lies wholly inside Allen County and covers **five of the county's thirteen civil subdivisions**: 11,390 people in [American Township](../place/american-township.yml), 4,849 in [Lima](../place/lima.yml), all 1,231 in [Sugar Creek Township](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml), 1,082 in [Marion Township](../place/marion-township.yml) and 324 in [Amanda Township](../place/amanda-township.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.

The township government whose territory is [Jackson Township](../place/jackson-township.yml). Its township house is at 225 Sugar Street, Lafayette, its telephone is 419.649.6482, and its trustees meet on the first and third Tuesday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

What the address file does carry is a fire department shared with the village: `LAFAYETTE & JACKSON TOWNSHIP FIRE DEPARTMENT IN LAFAYETTE AT 215 E SUGAR`, two doors from the township house address. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). Jackson is one of only two townships in the county lying entirely inside one school district; the other is Sugar Creek.

The county's largest school district by population and its smallest by area — 28,122 people over 8.745 square miles, internal point 40.739641, -84.112076, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population. At 3,200 people to the square mile it is more than seven times as dense as any other district touching the county; the next is Shawnee Local at 417.

**It is not the city, and the gap runs both ways.** It holds 27,821 of Lima's 35,579 people — 78 per cent — while the other 7,758 residents of the city are in four suburban districts. It also reaches outside the corporate boundary: 301 people in [American Township](../place/american-township.yml), and unpopulated blocks in Shawnee and Bath townships that are the trace of annexed ground the school boundary followed. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. The earlier form of this node said the boundary "does not follow the municipal or township lines around it. [inference] — from the area and internal point alone". It has now been compared against the places, and the inference holds in detail.

The township government whose territory is [Marion Township](../place/marion-township.yml). Its township house is at 5405 Kiggins Road, its telephone is 419.692.8846, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Monday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.814513, -84.319250, landmarked `MARION TOWNSHIP ROAD & POLICE DEPT`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**It has its own police force.** The county's address file landmarks the building at the township house address as `MARION TOWNSHIP ROAD & POLICE DEPT`. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). Three of the twelve townships here run police departments; the other nine are policed by the county sheriff.

The township government whose territory is [Monroe Township](../place/monroe-township.yml). Its township house is at 8500 Slabtown Road, its telephone is 419.641.5430, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Monday of the month at 7:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.861214, -84.051203, landmarked `MONROE TOWNSHIP HOUSE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

**Its township house has a Putnam County postal address.** The county gives it as `8500 Slabtown Road, Columbus Grove, Ohio 45833`, and Columbus Grove is a village in Putnam County. The building's coordinate is inside Monroe Township, in Allen County, and its `MUNI` is blank. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

A Putnam County district whose southern edge crosses into Allen — 3,502 people over 67.625 square miles, internal point 41.000054, -83.948062, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

3,463 of its people are in Putnam County and **39 in Allen**, across seven blocks in the north of [Richland Township](../place/richland-township.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block.

The smallest by population of the five districts lying wholly inside Allen County — 3,660 people over 33.598 square miles south-east of Lima, internal point 40.675113, -84.041425, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

**It contains no incorporated place and it is not rural.** 3,357 of its people are the whole of [Perry Township](../place/perry-township.yml) less 25, and the remaining 303 live inside the city of [Lima](../place/lima.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Those 303 are the smallest of the five slices Lima is cut into, and they are the reason this district is in the corpus as more than a name: a district with no village of its own still reaches into the county seat.

The township government whose territory is [Perry Township](../place/perry-township.yml). Its township house is at 2408 E. Breese Road, its telephone is 419.221.2412, and its trustees meet on the first and third Tuesday of the month at 7:30 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.687591, -84.060925, landmarked `PERRY TOWNSHIP ADMINISTRATION BUILDING`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

It runs an administration building at the township house address and a police department a hundred yards east at 2501 E Breese Road. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

The township government whose territory is [Richland Township](../place/richland-township.yml). Its township house is at 8435 N. Dixie Highway, its telephone is 419.358.4897, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Tuesday of the month at 8:00 p.m.. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

The county's address file puts the building at 40.862153, -83.934326, landmarked `RICHLAND TOWNSHIP GARAGE`, and that point falls inside the township. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

The county's address file landmarks the building at that address as `RICHLAND TOWNSHIP GARAGE` and nothing else — the only one of the twelve whose sole landmark is a works building rather than a hall, house or administration office. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

The county's third largest district — 17,056 people over 40.932 square miles south and west of Lima, internal point 40.700628, -84.180974, serving PK–12. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), unified school district file, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

It holds every one of [Shawnee Township](../place/shawnee-township.yml)'s 12,482 people, and more than a quarter of its own population lives elsewhere: 2,847 in [American Township](../place/american-township.yml), 1,033 inside [Lima](../place/lima.yml), 665 in [Amanda Township](../place/amanda-township.yml), and **29 across the line in Auglaize County**. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block. Those 29 people on four blocks are why this node no longer says its territory is within Allen County.

It contains [Fort Shawnee](../place/fort-shawnee.yml) and its 6,263 people — a third of the district, in a place with no municipal government of its own. [verified] — same source. The earlier form of this node called the boundary's disagreement with the township lines an inference from area and internal point; the comparison has now been made against the places themselves.

The township government whose territory is [Shawnee Township](../place/shawnee-township.yml). Its township house is at 2530 Ft. Amanda Road, its telephone is 419.991.8706, and its trustees meet on the second and fourth Monday of the month at 10:00 a.m. — the only board in the county that meets in the morning. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), townships page.

properties.parameter: natural population change, four years to 2024

blocks.text: Across the four full years 2021 to 2024 the county recorded **4,763 births and 5,269 deaths** — a natural change of **−506**. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), county file, fields `BIRTHS` and `DEATHS`.
Year by year the natural change was −213, −259, −41 and **+7**: deaths exceeded births in 2021, 2022 and 2023, and births exceeded deaths again in 2024. [verified] — same source.

**Deaths moved and births did not.** Births ran 1,171, 1,190, 1,202 and 1,200 — flat within three per cent. Deaths ran 1,384, 1,449, 1,243 and 1,193, peaking in 2022 and falling by 256 over the following two years. So the natural decrease of these four years is a deaths story, and the shape of it — a spike in 2021–2022 subsiding by 2024 — is the shape the pandemic left in county death counts across the United States. [inference] The corpus holds no cause-of-death data and cannot attribute it.

properties.method: Domestic plus international net migration, summed over the four full estimate years 2021–2024. The partial year 2020 is excluded as not comparable. [verified]

blocks.text: Across the four full years 2021 to 2024 the county's net migration was **−793**: a domestic net loss of **1,217** against an international net gain of **424**. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), county file, fields `DOMESTICMIG` and `INTERNATIONALMIG`.

**The two components move in opposite directions and one of them is accelerating.** International migration ran 26, 100, 133 and 165 — rising every year without exception. Domestic migration ran −213, −530, −317 and −157, worst in 2022 and shrinking since. [verified] — same source.

In 2024 they crossed: 165 arriving from abroad against 157 leaving for elsewhere in the United States, for a net migration of **+8** — the first non-negative year in the series. [verified] — same source.

blocks.text: Of 45,815 presidential votes cast in the county, **30,487 for Trump and 13,294 for Clinton** — 66.5 per cent against 29.0, with 1,486 for Johnson and 323 for Stein. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md), summed over the county's 88 precincts.

**Thirteen precincts went to Clinton**, twelve of them in [Lima](../place/lima.yml) and the thirteenth `AMERICAN D`, in the township wrapped around the city. Four years later [eleven went to Biden](allen-county-presidential-vote-2020.yml): `LIMA 1A` and `LIMA 1C` crossed over and nothing crossed the other way. [verified] — same source.

The 1,486 votes for Johnson are the largest third-party showing in the three elections this corpus holds — three times Jorgensen's 590 in 2020 on a similar total vote. [verified] — same source. What that means is not recorded here; it is the kind of thing two data points cannot carry.

blocks.text: Of 47,993 presidential votes cast in the county, **33,116 for Trump and Pence and 14,149 for Biden and Harris** — 69.0 per cent against 29.5, with 590 for Jorgensen and Cohen and 138 for Hawkins and Walker. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md).

**Eleven of the county's 88 precincts went to Biden, and ten of them are in Lima.** The eleventh is `AMERICAN D`, in the township wrapped around the city's west and north. Every other precinct in the county — all twelve townships' rural ground, both cities' outer wards, every village — went the other way. [verified] — same source. The most Republican precinct is `MONROE E` at 90.6 per cent; the most Democratic is `LIMA 6C` at 87.9. A county that votes 69–29 contains precincts ninety points apart.

**It is the third of three, and the county is drifting.** Republican share of the top-of-ticket vote ran 66.5 per cent in [2016](allen-county-presidential-vote-2016.yml), 67.3 in [2018](allen-county-governor-vote-2018.yml) and 69.0 here — a move of 2.5 points across two presidential elections, against a median precinct move of 1.5. [verified] — same source.

**Every precinct Clinton won in 2016 moved toward the Republicans**, all thirteen of them, by a mean of 4.5 points; `LIMA 1A` and `LIMA 1C` crossed over entirely. Across the 88 the correlation between 2016 Republican share and the 2016–2020 swing is **−0.39**: the more Democratic a precinct was, the harder it moved. [verified] — computed here from the three files.
Down-ballot in 2020, Jim Jordan took 33,201 to 13,080, Matt Huffman 34,303 to 12,645, and Bob Cupp ran unopposed with 38,882. [verified] — same source.

blocks.text: 48,353 ballots cast against 67,374 registered voters at the general election of 3 November 2020 — **71.8 per cent**, summed over the county's 88 precincts. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md).

**The county figure hides a fifty-two point spread.** Turnout ran from 35.4 per cent in `LIMA 3B` to 87.8 per cent in `DELPHOS 1B`. No other quantity this corpus holds varies that far across the county: population per housing unit runs 2.19 to 2.57, and land area per subdivision by a factor of four. [verified] — same source, precinct by precinct.

Registration itself varies as much and is the more interesting number. Across the 88 precincts registered voters run from 0.28 to 0.84 per resident, and the low end of that range is where the county's [group quarters](../question/who-lives-in-the-county-without-housing.yml) are. [verified] — same source against [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block population.

blocks.text: The 88 voting districts into which Allen County's 3,552 census blocks are divided in the 2020 geography, named. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) for the assignment and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), layer 58, for the names, populations, housing units and areas.

**The precinct grid nests inside the civil geography exactly.** Not one of the 88 crosses a county-subdivision line. [verified] — the assignment files crossed with TIGERweb block geography, block by block — the sharp contrast with [the school districts](../jurisdiction/), which cross county and township lines freely. [Lima](../place/lima.yml) holds 23 and [Sugar Creek Township](../place/sugar-creek-township.yml) holds [one](../division/voting-district-sugar-creek-2020.yml); their populations sum to 102,206, which is [the county's own enumeration](allen-county-population-2020-census.yml).

**A second, unrelated pipeline confirms the names.** The 88 the county board of elections used on its certified returns are identical, string for string, to the 88 the Census Bureau publishes. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md) against TIGERweb. That joins [turnout](allen-county-turnout-2020.yml) and [the vote](allen-county-presidential-vote-2020.yml) to census geography with no crosswalk, and those show the 88 are far from interchangeable.

blocks.text: Land area of Lima city in the 2020 geography. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio place file.

This figure is the one in this corpus most exposed to the boundary problem, and it is seeded partly to make that visible. A municipality's land area changes by annexation, so comparing it to a figure from another year without checking the annexations between them compares two different pieces of ground. That check is [boundary-comparability](../../skills/boundary-comparability.md), and the corpus holds no annexation events yet for it to read. This figure describes the **corporation's territory**, not the settlement in the ordinary sense: the Census Bureau tabulates Lima at the corporate boundary of the date, so what the number counts is whatever ground the [City of Lima](../jurisdiction/city-of-lima.yml) had annexed by then. [inference] The node therefore carries a `describes` edge to the jurisdiction as well as to the place. Both are true and they are not the same claim — the place is what the name denotes, and the jurisdiction is what the boundary encloses.

blocks.text: Land area of [Ohio House District 4](../division/ohio-house-district-4-2020.yml) in the 2020 geography. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), state legislative lower chamber file.

properties.mouth: 41.2875489, -84.3557802, in Defiance County. Joins the Maumee River. [inference]

blocks.text: The river that collects Allen County's drainage and carries it north to the Maumee at Defiance. [inference] It rises at 40.6669957, -83.8938286 and discharges at 41.2875489, -84.3557802 in Defiance County. [verified] — [USGS GNIS](../../catalog/gnis-domestic-names-ohio.md), feature 1065901. It gives its name to Auglaize Township in the county's south — one of the twelve townships recorded in the [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md). [verified]

Its significance to this corpus is directional. Allen County drains north to Lake Erie rather than south to the Ohio, and the Auglaize is the channel by which it does so. That single fact organizes a great deal: the county's swamp history, its canal, and the basin its water quality is accounted for in are all consequences of being on the Lake Erie side of the divide. [inference]

**It rises in this county**, at 40.6669957, -83.8938286 in Auglaize township — the township named after it. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), point-in-polygon. So Allen County is not merely drained by the Auglaize; it is the ground the river starts on. See [where the Auglaize rises](../question/where-the-auglaize-rises.yml). Its whole subbasin, `04100007`, is one of the seven that make up the Maumee's drainage; the four blocks of that township on [the Scioto side](scioto-river-basin.yml) drain the opposite way, so the divide and this river's source are in the same township. [verified] — [USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset](../../catalog/usgs-watershed-boundary.md).

The glacially-formed wetland that covered much of northwest Ohio until it was drained in the second half of the nineteenth century. Allen County lies at its southern margin, and its northern townships were within it. [inference]

It belongs in this corpus because it is the negative space in the county's settlement history: the swamp is why this part of Ohio was settled late relative to the south of the state, why the drainage tile and ditch systems are as extensive as they are, and why the land is as productive as it is now that they exist. [inference] It is also a feature that no longer exists as such, which is a thing this class must be able to hold — a natural-feature node is not required to describe present ground.

**It has no GNIS record.** No feature named "Great Black Swamp" appears anywhere in the 17,921 rows of the Ohio file. [verified] — [USGS GNIS](../../catalog/gnis-domestic-names-ohio.md). That is not because the gazetteer omits vanished features: it carries 56 `Swamp` features in Ohio and marks the drained ones "(historical)" in the name itself. The likelier reason is that GNIS names features with a locatable point, and a wetland that covered much of northwest Ohio across a dozen counties does not have one. [inference] So this node keeps no identifier, and the absence is a fact about how gazetteers work rather than a gap in the retrieval.

nodes.label: Maumee River Basin

blocks.text: The drainage basin that **almost all** of Allen County lies within — the largest watershed draining to the Great Lakes, discharging to Lake Erie at Toledo. 3,548 of the county's 3,552 census blocks and 102,107 of its 102,206 people are in the Great Lakes Region, across three subbasins: Auglaize `04100007` holds 3,200 blocks and Blanchard `04100008` holds 348. [verified] — [USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset](../../catalog/usgs-watershed-boundary.md), by block composition.

**This basin is not a hydrologic unit, which is why no code is recorded here.** The Maumee's drainage is seven subbasins — `04100003` St. Joseph through `04100009` Lower Maumee — and the next unit up that contains them, `041000` Western Lake Erie, also contains six that are nothing to do with the Maumee: Raisin, Sandusky, Huron and three more. [verified] — [USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset](../../catalog/usgs-watershed-boundary.md). So the honest answer to this node's genesis question about its own HUC is that it does not have one, and writing `0410` here would have named a basin four times too large.

**Its other genesis question is answered against it.** Part of Allen County does drain to the Ohio River: four blocks in [Auglaize Township](../place/auglaize-township.yml), 99 people, sit in [the Scioto basin](scioto-river-basin.yml). [verified] — same source. The corpus asserted the Lake Erie side for the whole county from genesis and flagged the southern townships as unchecked; checking them cost one query and moved 99 people to the Gulf of Mexico.

refusals: It is included at genesis for that reason: without it the trace from the Ottawa River runs to the Auglaize and stops in mid-air, and the corpus cannot say where its water goes.

properties.source: 41.0828261, -85.1321928 — the St. Joseph and St. Marys confluence, Fort Wayne.

blocks.text: The river Allen County's water reaches last before Lake Erie. It rises at 41.0828261, -85.1321928 — the confluence of the St. Joseph and St. Marys at Fort Wayne, Indiana — and discharges at 41.6994922, -83.4599325 at Toledo. [verified] — [USGS GNIS](../../catalog/gnis-domestic-names-ohio.md), feature 1084017.

The discharge coordinate is what makes the corpus's Lake Erie claim more than an assertion. Allen County's water leaves the county by the Auglaize, and the river the Auglaize joins ends at Toledo on Lake Erie rather than anywhere on the Ohio. [inference] — the coordinate is verified; that the Auglaize joins *this* river at Defiance is not established by a names file.

nodes.label: Ottawa River

properties.huc_code: 0410000703 Upper Ottawa River, 0410000705 Lower Ottawa River
properties.mouth: 40.9950509, -84.2413355, in Putnam County. Joins the Auglaize River. [inference]
properties.source: 40.7708852, -83.9557761 — the Hog Creek / Little Hog Creek confluence.

blocks.text: The stream that runs through Lima, and the county's principal watercourse. It begins at 40.7708852, -83.9557761 and discharges at 40.9950509, -84.2413355 in Putnam County. [verified] — [USGS GNIS](../../catalog/gnis-domestic-names-ohio.md), feature 1070882. That the discharge point is on the Auglaize remains [inference]: a names file gives a coordinate and never says what is at it.

**It does not begin east of the city; it begins at a confluence.** Its source coordinate is identical to the mouths GNIS records for [Hog Creek](hog-creek.yml) and [Little Hog Creek](little-hog-creek.yml), so the river's head is where those two creeks meet. [verified] — same source. The older name of the whole watercourse was Hog Creek, and the name now attaches to the upper tributary; GNIS is consistent with that and does not establish it. [inference]

**Allen County's own rows do not contain it.** GNIS files a stream under the county of its mouth, so the county's principal river is filed under Putnam and is absent from the 113 features listed for Allen. [verified] — same source.

The present name is shared with a larger, unrelated Ottawa River near Toledo — feature 1066879 in Lucas County against this one's 1070882. [verified] — same source. The collision is now resolvable by identifier rather than by care.

**Where its water goes is now sourced rather than assumed.** The river has two watersheds of its own — `0410000703` Upper Ottawa River and `0410000705` Lower Ottawa River — and both sit inside subbasin `04100007`, which is named for and drains to the [Auglaize](auglaize-river.yml). [verified] — [USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset](../../catalog/usgs-watershed-boundary.md). That settles the basin and not the confluence: the WBD says this water reaches the Auglaize and never says which stream it joins first. Those two Ottawa watersheds hold 47,578 of the county's people between them, 47 per cent, which is what it means to call this the county's principal watercourse.

Being the watercourse Lima grew on, it was also the receiving water for the refinery and the works — the environmental history of this stream and the industrial history of the city are the same subject. [inference]

refusals: The older name of the whole watercourse was Hog Creek, and the name now attaches to the upper tributary; GNIS is consistent with that and does not establish it.

blocks.text: The drainage basin of the Scioto River, which discharges to the Ohio River at Portsmouth and through it to the Gulf of Mexico. **Ninety-nine people in Allen County live in it.** [verified] — [USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset](../../catalog/usgs-watershed-boundary.md).

Every other block in the county, 3,548 of 3,552, is in the Great Lakes Region and drains to [the Maumee basin](maumee-river-basin.yml). [verified] — same source, by block composition; all 3,552 blocks land in exactly one subbasin and their populations sum to the county's own enumeration of 102,206.

The subwatershed those four blocks sit in is `050600010101`, **Cottonwood Ditch** — a headwater of the Scioto rising in Auglaize Township. [verified] — same source. It is the only named feature on the Ohio River side of the divide in this county.

The county's elected chief law enforcement officer, one of the separately elected county offices Ohio law establishes for every county. [inference] The sheriff runs the county jail and serves process in addition to policing the unincorporated area.

**Its line of holders is complete.** Thirty-nine tenures run from Henry Lippencott in 1831 to the present holder, with every term's end year equal to the next term's start year and no holder recorded twice in succession. [verified] — [Allen County Sheriff's Office past-sheriffs roster](../../catalog/acso-past-sheriffs.md); the continuity was checked across all thirty-nine entries rather than assumed, and is now checked by [`crates/succession`](../../../crates/succession/) on every test run rather than by hand.

Two features of the line are worth knowing before computing on it. John Keller held the office in 1835–1839 and again in 1843–1845, so the corpus carries one person and two tenures with `term_number` set. [verified] And the roster's ranges are year-only, so consecutive tenures share a boundary year; read as day-precision intervals every adjacent pair overlaps, and none of those overlaps is real.
The elected chief executive of the [City of Lima](../jurisdiction/city-of-lima.yml). [inference]
A private liberal arts university at [Bluffton](../place/bluffton.yml), with a Mennonite affiliation reflecting the Swiss Mennonite settlement of that part of the county. [inference]

**Its residential population is now a measured number.** Census block `390030101001002` holds 398 people in 2 housing units — a population living almost entirely outside housing, which is what a campus looks like in the block file. The county's address file puts Ropp Hall 0.02 miles from that block's internal point, with Bren Dell Hall, College Hall and Musselman Library inside 0.15. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block layer and [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). The 398 are students in residence on census day; they are not the university's enrolment, and the campus is not necessarily one block. [inference]

That block is in [Bluffton](../place/bluffton.yml) village, which settles by assignment rather than by inference where the university sits. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md).

The locomotive builder that made Lima's name in railroading. It began as a machine shop building the geared Shay locomotive under Ephraim Shay's patent — a design for logging and industrial railways that could work steep, rough, temporary track that a conventional rod locomotive could not. [inference]

It later became one of the three major American builders of mainline steam, and is associated with the "Super Power" concept — a design direction emphasising boiler capacity and free steaming that the company introduced in the mid-1920s. [inference]

The company that industrialized the Lima oil field after the 1885 strike. Standard Oil bought into the field, built refining capacity at Lima, and solved the problem that had made Lima crude nearly worthless — its high sulphur content, which fouled refining and gave the product the name "sour crude" — by acquiring a desulphurization process. [inference]

It matters to this corpus as the mechanism by which a local discovery became a national one. The strike made oil available; Standard made it saleable, and in doing so attached this county to a national industrial economy in a way its agriculture never had. [inference]

properties.character: Water transport as the organizing fact of the county's west, and a divided county economy. [inference]

blocks.text: The span in which [the Miami and Erie Canal](../site/miami-and-erie-canal.yml) was the organizing transport fact of western Allen County — roughly the 1840s to the end of the nineteenth century, when rail had comprehensively displaced it. [inference]

Its character is a geographic asymmetry rather than a countywide condition, and that is the reason it is worth naming as a period at all. The canal ran through the county's western edge and made [Delphos](../place/delphos.yml) and Spencerville into places; it did not touch Lima, which grew instead around a railway junction. So for several decades the county had two economies oriented to two different transport systems, and its later concentration on Lima is partly the story of one of them winning. [inference]

nodes.label: Deindustrialization

properties.character: Contraction of manufacturing employment and sustained population loss concentrated in the county seat. The population half is verified; the manufacturing half is not. [inference]

blocks.text: The span from roughly 1970 in which the county's manufacturing employment contracted and [Lima](../place/lima.yml) entered the sustained population decline it is still in. [inference]

**The decline is now demonstrated rather than asserted.** Allen County counted 111,144 at the 1970 census and 100,866 at the 2024 estimate — a loss of 10,278 people, or 9.2%, across five decades with no reversal at any measured point: 111,144 (1970), 108,464 (2000), 106,331 (2010), 102,217 (2020), 100,866 (2024). [verified] — see [1970](../measure/allen-county-population-1970.yml), [2000](../measure/allen-county-population-2000.yml), [2010](../measure/allen-county-population-2010.yml), [2020](../measure/allen-county-population-2020.yml) and [2024](../measure/allen-county-population-2024.yml). The arithmetic is this corpus's; every input is a Census figure.

**The concentration is now evidenced too, over one decade.** This node carries a `concentrated-in` edge to Lima, and between 2000 and 2010 Lima fell 3.8% while the balance of Allen County — everything outside every incorporated place — fell 1.5%, from 50,809 to 50,048. [verified] — [Census Intercensal Estimates, 2000–2010](../../catalog/census-intercensal-2000-2010.md). Lima declined about two and a half times as fast as the rest of the county. [inference]

**The mechanism, for the first time.** Across the four full years 2021 to 2024 the county lost 1,271 people: **506 to natural decrease and 793 to net migration**, with a residual of 28. [verified] — [natural change](../measure/allen-county-natural-change-2021-2024.yml) and [net migration](../measure/allen-county-net-migration-2021-2024.yml), both from the same Population Estimates file this node has cited since its second phase. More people leave than arrive, and more die than are born, and the first is the larger of the two.

**The decline is broad and uneven.** Between the 2020 estimates base and 2024, eleven of the county's thirteen civil subdivisions lost population. Lima lost most in absolute terms — 841 of a county loss of 1,351 — and the only two that grew were Auglaize township, by 55, and Marion township, by 102, at the county's south-eastern and Delphos ends. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. So this is not a city emptying into its own suburbs: the suburban ring is shrinking too, slower. [inference]

refusals: **What the evidence does not establish, stated plainly.** It does not establish that 1970 is the start.
It does not establish that either mechanism reaches back before 2020.

It does not establish that the decline has ended: fifteen people on 100,851 is far inside what a modelled estimate can resolve, one year is not a direction, and the same programme revises its own earlier years with every vintage.

The county itself, as ground rather than as government: 402.545 square miles of land and 4.306 square miles of water in the northwest quarter of Ohio, with an internal point at 40.771627, -84.106103. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md).

The land is glacial till plain, flat and poorly drained, and its northern reach lay within the Great Black Swamp until nineteenth-century drainage. [inference] That flatness is the reason the county's transport history runs through a canal and then a railway junction rather than through a river port: its streams drain north and west to the Auglaize and the Maumee and were never navigable here.

**It is three places.** Lima holds 35,531 people; the three townships wrapped around it — [American](american-township.yml) 14,571, [Shawnee](shawnee-township.yml) 12,509 and [Bath](bath-township.yml) 9,399 — hold 36,479 between them, more than the city; and the other nine townships hold about thirty thousand across roughly five hundred square miles. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. That suburban middle is largely outside any municipality: Shawnee Township contains no incorporated place at all. [verified] — same source.

A township of 33.315 square miles about 9 miles west of the county's centre, internal point 40.734865, -84.272548. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio county subdivisions.

Its population was 2,070 at the 2020 estimates base and 2,049 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. Its population fell by 21 over those four years, as all but two of the county's subdivisions did.
It contains no incorporated place; all of it is unincorporated. [verified] — same source, which lists no place within this township.

**No school district is named for it and three divide it**: 1,072 of its people are in [Spencerville Local](../jurisdiction/spencerville-local-school-district.yml), 665 in [Shawnee Local](../jurisdiction/shawnee-local-school-district.yml) and 324 in [Elida Local](../jurisdiction/elida-local-school-district.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block geography. A township with no village and no district of its own has no institution that takes its name as a whole, which is worth knowing before reading anything into how little is written about it.
A township of 24.017 square miles wrapping the west and north of Lima, internal point 40.769378, -84.17822. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md).

It is the most populous township in the county outside Lima itself, and the Census Bureau's "balance of American township" figure — the township minus the incorporated villages inside it — is the larger part of that. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. Its population was 14,571 at the 2020 estimates base and 14,445 in 2024 — **the most populous civil subdivision in the county after Lima**, and 12,541 of the 2024 figure is the balance outside [Elida](elida.yml), the one village in it. [verified] — same source.

**Neither the refinery nor the tank plant is here.** This node claimed both stand on or near its boundary with Lima, and therefore that this township holds most of the county's heavy industry. Both are in [Shawnee Township](shawnee-township.yml), south of Lima; this township wraps Lima's west and north. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), agreeing independently on both points. The claim is withdrawn entire rather than narrowed: it named two sites and was wrong about both.
It does hold a fifth of [census tract 39003010300](../division/census-tract-39003010300.yml) — 13,403,443 square metres and 408 people. [verified] — same source, block composition.

A township of 35.99 square miles about 11 miles south-east of the county's centre, internal point 40.695518, -83.928053. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio county subdivisions.

Its population was 2,764 at the 2020 estimates base and 2,819 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. It is one of only two subdivisions in the county that grew over those four years, by 55.

Its schools are split: 2,740 of its people are in [Allen East Local](../jurisdiction/allen-east-local-school-district.yml) and 17, on two blocks at the south-east corner, in Auglaize County's [Waynesfield-Goshen](../jurisdiction/waynesfield-goshen-local-school-district.yml). [verified] — same source, crossed with [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block geography.

**The continental divide runs through it.** Four of its census blocks — 99 people and 43 housing units, along the county's eastern edge between 40.6487 and 40.7104 north — are in [the Scioto basin](../natural-feature/scioto-river-basin.yml) and drain to the Ohio River and the Gulf of Mexico. Delphos straddles the Allen–Van Wert county line, and the Census Bureau's Allen County rows record it as `Delphos city (pt.)` for exactly that reason: the 3,941 counted there in the 2020 estimates base is the Allen County portion, not the city. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md). Any figure for Delphos taken from an Allen County table and reported as the city's population understates it. [inference] See [the Miami and Erie Canal](../site/miami-and-erie-canal.yml). **It was four towns before it was one.** The county records Delphos as originally Howard, Section Ten, West Bredeick and East Bredeick, merged into a single town in 1851. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page. **Its schools are not one system.** The city's 35,579 people at the 2020 census divide among five school districts: 27,821 in [Lima City](../jurisdiction/lima-city-school-district.yml), 4,849 in [Elida Local](../jurisdiction/elida-local-school-district.yml), 1,573 in [Bath Local](../jurisdiction/bath-local-school-district.yml), 1,033 in [Shawnee Local](../jurisdiction/shawnee-local-school-district.yml) and 303 in [Perry Local](../jurisdiction/perry-local-school-district.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block geography, block by block. A fifth of the city is outside the district that carries its name — the shape annexation leaves when the school boundaries do not move with the corporate one.

**Founded in 1831**, and the county seat. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page — which puts it on Interstate 75 about 72 miles north of Dayton and 78 south of Toledo, the county's own way of saying where it is.

**It is also where the county's minority vote lives, and where it is shrinking fastest.** Eleven of Allen County's 88 precincts went to Biden in 2020 and ten of them are here; the county as a whole went 69 to 29 the other way. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md). The city holds a third of the county's people, most of its density, five school districts and 23 of its 88 precincts, and on every one of those measures it is the part that does not resemble the rest.

Between 2016 and 2020 its 23 precincts moved toward the Republicans by a mean of **3.2 points** while the county's other 65 moved 1.6 — the city drifting right about twice as fast as the ground around it, from a much more Democratic starting point. [verified] — same source, computed across three general elections. So the county's political division is narrowing from the city's side, which is the opposite of the direction its [population decline](../period/deindustrialization.yml) runs.
Pronounced LY-muh, not like the Peruvian capital. [inference]

A township of 42.371 square miles about 10 miles west of the county's centre, internal point 40.81041, -84.292789. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio county subdivisions.

Its population was 6,629 at the 2020 estimates base and 6,731 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. It is one of only two subdivisions in the county that grew over those four years, by 102.
It contains [Delphos](delphos.yml). [verified] — same source, which reports it as a place within this township.

A township of 36.094 square miles about 7 miles north of the county's centre, internal point 40.864357, -84.060914. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio county subdivisions.

Its population was 2,050 at the 2020 estimates base and 2,005 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. Its population fell by 45 over those four years, as all but two of the county's subdivisions did. That makes it the 11th most populous of the county's thirteen civil subdivisions.
It contains [Cairo](cairo.yml). [verified] — same source, which reports it as a place within this township.

Three school districts divide it, and one of them is not an Allen County district at all: 1,129 of its people are in [Bath Local](../jurisdiction/bath-local-school-district.yml), 489 in Putnam County's [Columbus Grove Local](../jurisdiction/columbus-grove-local-school-district.yml), and 449 in [Bluffton Exempted Village](../jurisdiction/bluffton-exempted-village-school-district.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block geography.
