Its population was 3,377 at the 2020 estimates base and 3,333 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. Its population fell by 44 over those four years, as all but two of the county's subdivisions did.
It contains no incorporated place; all of it is unincorporated. [verified] — same source, which lists no place within this township.

A township of 41.648 square miles about 11 miles north-east of the county's centre, internal point 40.869365, -83.936562. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio county subdivisions.

Its population was 5,889 at the 2020 estimates base and 5,775 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. Its population fell by 114 over those four years, as all but two of the county's subdivisions did.
It contains [Beaverdam](beaverdam.yml) and [Bluffton](bluffton.yml). [verified] — same source, which reports them as places within this township.
A township of 28.97 square miles immediately south and west of Lima, internal point 40.691353, -84.170464. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md).

Its name records the Shawnee presence on this ground before the cession, and it is the clearest surviving toponymic trace of it in the county's civil geography. [inference] With 12,509 people at the 2020 estimates base and 12,490 in 2024 it is the county's second most populous civil subdivision after Lima — and it **contains no incorporated place at all**. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file, which lists no place row under this township. Twelve and a half thousand people live here under township government and no municipal one.

**It holds the county's heavy industry**, which the corpus attributed to Lima at genesis and to [American Township](american-township.yml) alongside it. Both the [refinery](../site/lima-refinery.yml) and the [tank plant](../site/lima-army-tank-plant.yml) stand on unincorporated ground in this township, with Lima postal addresses and no municipality. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

That is a fact about tax base and authority as much as geography: the two largest industrial installations in the county are outside every municipality that could levy on them, and the township is the government whose ground they sit on. [inference]

A township of 23.308 square miles about 14 miles west of the county's centre, internal point 40.732439, -84.371928. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio county subdivisions.

Its population was 3,058 at the 2020 estimates base and 2,998 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. Its population fell by 60 over those four years, as all but two of the county's subdivisions did.
It contains [Spencerville](spencerville.yml). [verified] — same source, which reports it as a place within this township.

A village of 0.965 square miles in [Spencer Township](spencer-township.yml), about 14 miles west of the county's centre, internal point 40.707965, -84.353159. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), Ohio places.

Its population was 2,205 at the 2020 estimates base and 2,164 in 2024. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file. It lost 41 people over those four years.

**All of it is in Allen County.** The same file marks a place that crosses a county line with `(pt.)` and marks this one plainly, which is what separates it from [Bluffton](bluffton.yml) and [Delphos](delphos.yml). [verified] — same source.

**Founded in 1844 on the banks of the [Miami and Erie Canal](../site/miami-and-erie-canal.yml).** [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page. That verifies for this village what the canal node had only inferred about the two canal towns, and it dates the settlement to the canal's own working decade.

The **smallest of the county's thirteen civil subdivisions by population** and among its smallest by area — 24.094 square miles, internal point 40.824171, -84.173843. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md). Its 2020 estimates base was 1,226 and its 2024 estimate 1,197, a twelfth of American Township's on comparable ground, and it contains no incorporated place. [verified] — [Census Population Estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md), sub-county file.

It contains one settlement, [Gomer](gomer.yml), whose 345 people are 28 per cent of the township — a census designated place, so the claim above that it holds no *incorporated* place still stands. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md). It is also one of only two townships in the county that a single school district covers entire; every block of it is in [Elida Local](../jurisdiction/elida-local-school-district.yml), a district named for a village three miles south of this township and not in it. [verified] — same source, crossed with [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) block geography.

An unincorporated community of 1.821 square miles in the south-east of the county, internal point 40.701038, -83.975081, with 406 people at the 2020 census. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md), where it is listed as `Westminster CDP`, and [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md) for the count.

It lies wholly within [Auglaize Township](auglaize-township.yml) — all fourteen of its census blocks do — and holds 15 per cent of that township's 2,757 people. [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md) crossed with TIGERweb block geography. The generous test that county subdivisions merely *intersecting* it returns two townships, Auglaize and Perry; the block composition returns one. The difference is a shared boundary line, and it is why containment here is settled by counting blocks rather than by asking a spatial query.

nodes.label: Which congressional district is Allen County in now?

properties.would_close_this: A current county-to-congressional-district relationship file from the Census Bureau, if one is published for the 118th or 119th Congress under a path this corpus has not found; the Ohio Secretary of State's district map, retrieved by hand rather than by an automated client; or the enacted redistricting plan itself, which names its constituent counties.

blocks.text: At the 2020 census, all 3,552 of Allen County's census blocks fell in [Ohio's 4th congressional district](../division/ohio-congressional-district-4-2020.yml). [verified] — [2020 Census Block Assignment Files](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md).

refusals: The corpus does not know the county's current district and does not guess it.

nodes.label: Who is Allen County named for?

properties.would_close_this: The text of the 1820 act erecting the county, or contemporaneous legislative journals from the Ohio General Assembly session that passed it. A county history asserting the attribution is not sufficient on its own: local histories are the origin of both candidates and repeat each other.

blocks.text: The county's name is not securely attributed. The two candidates usually offered are [John Allen](../person/john-allen.yml), a Kentucky colonel killed at the River Raisin in 1813, and Ethan Allen of Vermont. [inference]

nodes.label: What was Allen County's population before 1970, and when did Lima peak?

properties.would_close_this: For the county, the Census publication "Population of States and Counties of the United States: 1790–1990" (a 14.9MB PDF located but not read), or the 1900 Ohio bulletin "Population of Ohio by Counties and Minor Civil Divisions" for the nineteenth-century series. For Lima, a place-level decennial series — the 1970 and 1980 Census of Population volumes for Ohio, which the county-level file used here does not cover.

blocks.text: Allen County's population is on record at 111,144 in 1970 and 100,866 in 2024, and Lima's at 40,307 in 2000. [verified] — [1970–1979 county estimates](../../catalog/census-county-estimates-1970s.md), [Vintage 2024 estimates](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md) and [2000–2010 intercensal estimates](../../catalog/census-intercensal-2000-2010.md). No source reaching earlier than those has been retrieved, so the corpus's county series begins at 1970 and its Lima series at 2000 — see [the 1970 census count](../measure/allen-county-population-1970.yml).

refusals: The corpus holds no Lima figure earlier than 2000 and therefore cannot say when the city was largest, though it names a period beginning in 1970 partly on that basis.

nodes.label: What happened at the two irregular sheriff transitions?

properties.would_close_this: Allen County commissioners' journals or common pleas records for 1933 and 2017, which record a vacancy and its filling; or contemporary Lima newspaper coverage, which would date and explain both. For the 2017 case, the county's own record of the appointment.

blocks.text: The [past-sheriffs roster](../../catalog/acso-past-sheriffs.md) is continuous from 1831 to the present with no gaps and no overlaps. [verified] Two of its thirty-nine entries are nonetheless irregular in a way the source does not explain, and both have an obvious reading the corpus declines to write down.

nodes.label: What happened to the Village of Fort Shawnee?

properties.would_close_this: Ohio Secretary of State or Allen County records of municipal dissolution, or the county's own list of political subdivisions; alternatively the Census Bureau's Boundary and Annexation Survey for the relevant year, which records why a place's status changed and would distinguish a dissolution from a reclassification directly.

blocks.text: [Fort Shawnee](../place/fort-shawnee.yml) is listed by the Census Bureau as `Fort Shawnee village` with a population of 3,866 in 2000 and 3,726 in 2010, as `Fort Shawnee CDP` in the 2020 Gazetteer, and not at all in the Vintage 2024 sub-county file. [verified] — [2020 Census Gazetteer](../../catalog/census-gazetteer-2020.md) and [Census Intercensal Estimates, 2000–2010](../../catalog/census-intercensal-2000-2010.md).

refusals: So something changed between the 2010 and 2020 geographies, and the corpus does not know what.

nodes.label: When was Allen County's government organized?

properties.would_close_this: The Ohio General Assembly act organizing the county, or the first volume of the Allen County commissioners' or common pleas records, whose opening date bounds the answer directly.

blocks.text: [The county was laid out in 1820](../event/erection-of-allen-county.yml), but under Ohio practice a county could exist on paper for years before it had its own courts and officers, being attached to a neighbouring county in the meantime. [inference] The corpus places the organization about a decade later without a source. [inference]

**Corroborating evidence has since arrived, and does not close this.** The Allen County Sheriff's Office's own roster records Henry Lippencott as sheriff from 1831 — the earliest dated act of county government anywhere in this corpus. [verified] — [past-sheriffs roster](../../catalog/acso-past-sheriffs.md). A county with an elected sheriff is a county with a functioning government, so 1831 is now a firm *upper* bound on the organization date and strong support for the decade the corpus had guessed. [inference]

nodes.label: Does the Auglaize River rise in Allen County?

properties.resolution: Point-in-polygon against TIGERweb's 2020 county and county-subdivision layers. The source is in Allen County, Ohio, in Auglaize township — the township named for the river.
properties.would_close_this: A county boundary polygon checked against the source coordinate. Closed by exactly that.

blocks.text: **Yes, and in the township named after it.** The river's source coordinate, 40.6669957, -83.8938286, falls inside Allen County, Ohio — GEOID `39003` — and inside Auglaize township, GEOID `3900302988`, in census tract 115. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), point-in-polygon against the 2020 county and county-subdivision layers. The source coordinate is [USGS GNIS](../../catalog/gnis-domestic-names-ohio.md) feature 1065901. [verified]

So Allen County is not merely drained by the Auglaize. It is the ground the river starts on, and the township that carries the river's name is the one it rises in — which is the ordinary direction for a name to travel and is worth having checked rather than assumed. [inference]

nodes.label: Who are the 1,360 people in a Lima block with no housing units?

properties.would_close_this: The Ohio Department of Rehabilitation and Correction's facility list, which gives each institution's current name, address and population; or the Census Bureau's group-quarters tabulation from the 2020 redistricting file, which reports institutional population by type and is not served by TIGERweb.

blocks.text: Two census blocks in Allen County hold a substantial population and essentially no housing units, which by the Census Bureau's own definitions means their residents are in **group quarters** rather than households. Together they hold 1,758 people, 1.7 per cent of the county. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), block layer, `POP100` against `HU100`.

**One is settled.** Block `390030101001002` holds 398 people in 2 housing units, and the county's address file puts [Bluffton University](../organization/bluffton-university.yml)'s Ropp Hall 0.02 miles from its internal point with five more university buildings inside 0.15. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md).

**The other is not.** Block `390030112001004` holds **1,360 people in zero housing units** over 0.141 square miles, inside [Lima](../place/lima.yml) and in precinct `LIMA 1A`. Exactly one county address point falls within it and its landmark reads `BIBLE ROAD AUTO WRECKING AT 505 BIBLE RD`. [verified] — same two sources, the address points projected out of State Plane and tested against the block polygon.

The county's three state correctional institutions — `ALLEN CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTE` and `LIMA CORRECTIONAL INSTITUTE` at 2338 and 2350 N West St, `OAKWOOD CORRECTIONAL FACILITY` at 3200 N West St — are in the same precinct and in adjacent blocks, about half a mile west. [verified] — same source. That an institution's single address point sits at its gate while its residents are counted in the block holding the buildings would explain the whole discrepancy. [inference] It is an inference and not a finding: nothing retrieved here names what stands on those ninety acres.

**A third source now agrees with the first two and still does not answer them.** The precinct containing that block, [`LIMA 1A`](../division/voting-district-lima-1a-2020.yml), has 908 registered voters against 3,240 residents — 0.28 per resident, the lowest of the county's 88 against a median of 0.68 and a next-lowest of 0.54. Take the 1,360 out and the ratio is 0.48, inside the range the rest of the county occupies. [verified] — [OpenElections](../../catalog/openelections-ohio.md) against [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md).

A census count, a housing count and a registration roll therefore agree that these residents are present without households and without registering. Three measurements of the same absence is not a name. [inference]

The seat of county government at Lima — the building the [county government](../jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml) occupies and the physical expression of Lima's status as county seat. [inference]

It stands at 301 N Main Street, 40.7430708, -84.1051751, and the county records its `MUNI` as Lima. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). The Census Bureau puts the same point in Lima city, GEOID `3943554`. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md). This is the one site of the three checked whose `located-in` edge was right all along, and it was checked anyway — a corpus that only tests the claims it doubts learns nothing about the ones it trusts.

nodes.label: Joint Systems Manufacturing Center (Lima Army Tank Plant)

properties.address: 1151 Buckeye Road, Lima OH 45804 — a postal address, not a municipality.

blocks.text: The government-owned tank plant south of Lima — the only facility in the United States that builds main battle tanks, producing and rebuilding the M1 Abrams under contractor operation. [inference] It stands at 40.6994478, -84.137903 and is registered as `United States Army Joint Systems Manufacturing Center Lima`, feature class Military. [verified] — [USGS GNIS](../../catalog/gnis-domestic-names-ohio.md), feature 2512481.

**It is not in Lima.** The plant stands in [Shawnee Township](../place/shawnee-township.yml), GEOID `3900371955`, and no incorporated place and no census designated place contains it — not Lima, and not the [Fort Shawnee](../place/fort-shawnee.yml) CDP a mile and a half away. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md), point-in-polygon against the 2020 county-subdivision, incorporated-place and CDP layers. The `located-in` edge points at the township accordingly; it named Lima from genesis until this was checked.

The county says so too, from its own data and by a different route: its address file records the plant at 1151 Buckeye Road with `USPS_CITY` "LIMA" and `MUNI` **blank**. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). Two agencies, two geometries, one answer.

Two claims here were wrong in the same direction. This node said the plant is on Lima's **northern** edge and it is 2.84 miles south of Lima's internal point, in another township entirely; and [American Township](../place/american-township.yml) said the plant stands on or near *its* boundary with Lima, which wraps Lima's west and north. The plant is south of the city and on neither. [verified] — same source.

It is government-owned and contractor-operated, which is why its `operated-by` edges point at both a jurisdiction and a company in principle; only the ownership side is asserted here, because the operating contractor is a corporate relationship this corpus has not sourced and which has changed hands. [inference]

Its presence makes Allen County's industrial base unusual in a specific way: the plant's workload is set by federal procurement rather than by any regional market, so the county has a major employer whose fortunes are decoupled from the deindustrialization that shaped the rest of its economy. [inference]
The locomotive erecting shops at Lima, where the Shay geared locomotives and later the mainline steam locomotives were built. [inference]

The plant has a node distinct from [the company](../organization/lima-locomotive-works.yml) because the two ended differently: the corporate identity was merged away in the mid-twentieth century while the physical works continued under other ownership building other products. Collapsing them would make the company's disappearance look like the site's, which is not what happened. [inference]

properties.address: 1150 S Metcalf Street, Lima OH 45804 — a postal address, not a municipality.

blocks.text: The petroleum refinery at Lima, built to process the crude of the Lima field after the 1885 strike and still operating. [inference] It is the longest-running industrial installation in the county and has outlived every corporate arrangement that has owned it.

**It has a Lima address and is not in Lima.** The county's address file records it at 1150 S Metcalf Street with `USPS_CITY` "LIMA" and `MUNI` **blank**, at 40.7221100, -84.1134691. [verified] — [Allen County GIS](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md). The Census Bureau, asked the same point independently, puts it in [Shawnee Township](../place/shawnee-township.yml) and in no incorporated place. [verified] — [TIGERweb](../../catalog/tigerweb-census2020.md). The `located-in` edge named Lima from genesis until both authorities were asked.

The state canal running between the Ohio River at Cincinnati and Lake Erie at Toledo, passing through the western edge of Allen County by way of [Delphos](../place/delphos.yml) and Spencerville. [inference]

It is a site rather than a natural feature because it was dug, and it is a site with an extent rather than a point — which is the case this class is defined to cover. Its significance here is that it gave the western townships a transport connection decades before the railways arrived. **Spencerville is verified to be one of its towns**: the county records it as founded in 1844 on the banks of this canal. [verified] — [Allen County](../../catalog/allen-county-official-site.md), cities and villages page. Delphos is not — the same page describes it as four towns merging in 1851 and does not mention the canal — so the claim that the canal is why *both* towns stand where they do is halved: verified for one, still an inference for the other. [inference]

The canal was superseded by rail and abandoned as a commercial route in the early twentieth century. [inference] Lima, notably, is not on it — the county's later industrial centre grew around a railway junction instead, which is part of why the canal towns and the county seat have such different nineteenth-century trajectories. [inference]

**GNIS names it and this node declines its coordinate.** The canal is feature 1057843, filed under Henry County with a primary coordinate at 41.3269935, -84.1943905 and a source of `0.0, 0.0`. [verified] — [USGS GNIS](../../catalog/gnis-domestic-names-ohio.md). That primary point is about 34 miles north of Delphos [inference], because a names file gives one coordinate per feature and this feature is a 250-mile canal. Writing it into `coordinates` would put the Delphos reach in Henry County, and writing the source into anything would put a canal in the Gulf of Guinea. The identifier is worth keeping; the coordinate is not.
